blocks.html: A witness is not credible, nor worthy of faith, who does not render a reason for his saying, a of which the Judge or the commissioner ought to interrogate him b; otherwise, if the commissioner has been so gross as not to ask it, the witness is not bound to render it c2, because he ought not to show himself eager [affectionné] to answer upon that on which he is not required or sought d. Nevertheless the witness also does no ill if he renders a reason voluntarily and of himself, without being interrogated upon it. Nay, in criminal matters (of which we treat here) the witness is bound to give a reason, even though he be not required to; otherwise his saying makes no faith f.

notes.citation: Code 4.20.4 (De testibus, l. Solam; Carus, Carinus and Numerian: Solam testationem prolatam nec aliis legitimis adminiculis causa approbatam…, a single deposition unsupported by other lawful aids is of no moment)
Decretals, X 2.20.37 (De testibus et attestationibus, c. Cum causam)
notes.original: c. cum cau ſam. de teſti.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.27.16 (De sententia et re iudicata, c. Sicut); the said c. Cum causam (X 2.20.37, note b); Accursius (Accur.), the Gloss on the said l. Solam (C. 4.20.4)

notes.citation: Code 1.19.8 (De precibus imperatori offerendis), the last law of the title (Theodosius and Valentinian, Instrumentorum exempla non prosit precibus adiunxisse…)
